title: Goat and Compass
venue_description:
Overview

Nestled in the heart of Wilmington's vibrant Brooklyn Arts District - Goat and Compass Pub brings a slice of traditional English pub culture to North Carolina. Owned by Scott Wagner and his team - this venue has become a cherished local gem where the community comes to unplug and connect in an authentic - welcoming atmosphere.

Atmosphere and Setting

The pub features a cozy wood-adorned interior that evokes classic English pub charm - complemented by a dog-friendly outdoor beer garden that's perfect for relaxing on pleasant days. Both spaces are designed for conversation and camaraderie - creating an environment where locals and visitors alike feel immediately at home. The venue strikes a perfect balance between casual comfort and character-filled ambiance.

Live Music and Events

Goat and Compass has established itself as a hub for local musical talent in Wilmington. The venue hosts the popular Hourglass Studios Open Mic Night every Tuesday - where musicians of all levels can perform in a supportive environment. Sign-ups start at 6:30pm with performances running from 7:00pm to 10:15pm. As an added incentive - performers are entered into a quarterly drawing to win 8 hours of free studio time at Hourglass Studios.

Beyond open mic nights - the venue regularly features live music showcases highlighting local artists. The performance calendar also includes lively trivia evenings - making it a versatile entertainment destination throughout the week.

Food and Drink

The pub has become famous for its signature bacon-infused vodka - a unique creation that perfectly captures the venue's creative spirit. Beer enthusiasts will appreciate the curated selection of over 15 beers on tap - featuring the best of Wilmington's local brewery scene. The full bar offers a range of spirits and specialty cocktails - while bar food and occasional food trucks provide sustenance for patrons.

Community Connection

What sets Goat and Compass apart is its role as a true community gathering place. The friendly staff - led by professional and attentive bartenders - creates a welcoming atmosphere that encourages both regulars and first-time visitors to settle in and stay awhile. The dog-friendly policy adds to the relaxed - inclusive vibe that defines the venue. Located on pedestrian-friendly 4th Street in the Brooklyn Arts District - the pub is easily accessible and surrounded by other local attractions - microbreweries and cultural venues.

Practical Information

The venue operates with flexible hours - typically opening at 5:00pm on weekdays and offering extended hours on weekends (until 2:00am Friday and Saturday). Both indoor and outdoor seating options are available - with TVs inside for sports viewing. Street parking is recommended as the best option for guests. While payment options include cash and cards - Apple Pay is not currently accepted.

title: Barzarre
venue_description:
Overview

Established in 2004 - Barzarre stands as Wilmington's most eclectic bohemian art bar and performance venue - a true hidden gem that has retained the gritty charm of old Wilmington while creating a completely unique entertainment experience. Located at the fringe of downtown on Castle Street - this unusual establishment defies easy categorization - functioning as a full bar - cafe - hookah lounge - taco joint and fringe performance venue all in one.

Atmosphere and Character

Barzarre exudes a bohemian world-traveler aesthetic with a secret speakeasy feel. The venue attracts an eclectic mix of artists - performers - musicians - bookworms - beer enthusiasts and curiosity-seekers who appreciate its unconventional charm. The atmosphere is simultaneously gritty and welcoming - with walls adorned in art and memorabilia - creating an environment where the unexpected is celebrated and creativity flourishes.

Music and Performance Events

The venue hosts an absolutely wild assortment of live entertainment spanning every possible genre. Live performances range from rock bands and acoustic acts to DJs - circus sideshows - burlesque - belly dance - fire shows - comedy and experimental performances. Barzarre proudly declares that entertainment ranges from 'Rock to Accordion - Burlesque to Ballet - Comedy to Klezmer - funk to folk and far more.'

Open Mic Mondays: The weekly Open Mic event is legendary in Wilmington - featuring music - comedy - spoken word - poetry - hip hop - improv and odd talents. Sign-ups start at 7:00pm and the show runs late. The event is truly 'nearly anything goes' - welcoming improvisational - raw or polished acts of all genres. Even guest chefs can participate through 'Open Mouth' - an open forum for culinary experimentation. Video screen and projector with HDMI hookups are ready for multimedia presentations. Touring musical acts often appear for featured sets.

Additional Music Events: Beyond Open Mic Mondays - Barzarre hosts a weekly drum circle in the back grotto patio starting at 7pm. There's also a regular circus and flow arts meetup where performers can share tricks - practice moves and connect with like-minded artists. Extra percussion is provided for newcomers to the drum circle.

Food and Drink

Barzarre offers an impressive beverage selection with a full liquor bar featuring specialty cocktails - over 170 craft beers - spiked seltzers - kombuchas and D9 drinks. There's always a $2 special to keep things affordable. The venue has teamed up with Incognito Barrito to create a popular taco menu with $3.50 tacos available until 8pm or until they run out. Customers can call ahead to have orders ready for pickup.

The cafe aspect of the venue offers additional food options - while the hookah lounge provides over 100 hookah blends for patrons who enjoy flavored tobacco. A street bar window allows for quick drink pickup - either for on-site enjoyment or to-go.

Venue Spaces

The venue features multiple areas for entertainment and relaxation. The main interior space hosts performances on a full stage with professional sound and lighting. Three outdoor patios provide additional gathering spaces - including the back grotto where the drum circle meets. The patios offer a perfect spot to chill between performances or enjoy drinks in a more relaxed setting.

Schedule and Operations

Barzarre is open every day from noon until at least midnight - with extended hours until 2am on weekends. The flexible schedule ensures there's always something happening - whether it's scheduled performances or spontaneous gatherings. The venue maintains an active events calendar with regularly scheduled showcases and one-off special events.

Community and Culture

What makes Barzarre truly special is its role as a gathering place for Wilmington's alternative and arts community. The venue has cultivated a reputation as the place where the weird - wonderful and experimental can thrive. Everyone is welcome - from seasoned performers to first-timers looking to try something new. The supportive atmosphere encourages artistic risk-taking and creative expression in all forms.

Practical Information

With a capacity of 100+ - Barzarre maintains an intimate feel while accommodating substantial crowds for popular events. Drink prices are intentionally kept affordable to remain accessible to the arts community. The venue is located in the historic district near downtown Wilmington - making it an easy walk from many downtown locations. Social media - particularly Instagram - is the best way to stay updated on upcoming events and special performances.

title: The Rusty Nail
venue_description:
Overview

The Rusty Nail stands as one of Wilmington's most authentic and beloved blues venues - a true juke joint that has been serving the community since 1957. For over a quarter century - this unassuming club has been the home of the Cape Fear Blues Society and host to the legendary Cape Fear Blues Jam - making it a cornerstone of the region's vibrant blues scene.

Atmosphere and Setting

Stepping into The Rusty Nail is like entering another era. The low-slung ceiling - late-1950s linoleum flooring and rotating vinyl-clad barstools create an atmosphere that conjures memories of when jukin' was king and blues legends ruled the scene. It's described as a little bit of Memphis and a whole lot of Chicago - wrapped up in a friendly Wilmington dive bar package. Walls adorned with blues memorabilia tell the story of decades of musical history - while a couple of billiard tables add to the classic saloon vibe.

Cape Fear Blues Jam

The Cape Fear Blues Jam is the heart and soul of The Rusty Nail - taking place every Tuesday at 8pm and on the first Saturday of each month at 8pm. This is not just any jam session - it's a true musical institution that has welcomed tens of thousands of participants since its formalization in 1996. The jam operates on a simple but powerful principle: any musician who walks through the door is invited to perform.

What sets this jam apart is the quality of equipment and organization. The Cape Fear Blues Society owns every piece of backline equipment and continuously maintains and updates it. Musicians have access to Fender Hot Rod and Peavey Delta Blues amplifiers - PDP/DW drums - Sabian cymbals - a Peavey bass rig - Shure microphones and a full professional PA system operated by a qualified soundman who doubles as the evening's jam master. This level of professional equipment in a jam setting is rare and demonstrates the society's commitment to providing the best possible experience for musicians.

Regular participants include talented local acts like Rose Lucas - Randy McQuay and RootSoul Project. The jam is known for its openness - accessibility and welcoming atmosphere - making it suitable for blues musicians of all skill levels. The quality and structure have attracted increasing numbers over the years - with attendance mirroring the venue's commitment to excellence.

Cape Fear Blues Festival

The Rusty Nail serves as the main venue for the annual Cape Fear Blues Festival - one of the longest-running blues events in the Carolinas. Launched in 1996 by the Cape Fear Blues Society - this three-day festival typically takes place in June and features performances on the indoor stage - outdoor tent stage and beer garden. The festival attracts touring blues artists - regional performers and local musicians - offering a mix of Delta - Chicago - Piedmont and contemporary blues styles. The outdoor tent events welcome lawn chairs but prohibit coolers and pets.

Venue Spaces

The intimate interior features small cocktail tables perfect for enjoying performances up close - creating a cozy living room-like atmosphere where friends gather around great music. Behind the club - a seasonal outdoor patio provides additional space - particularly utilized during festival events and warmer months. The venue's layout ensures that whether inside or outside - every seat offers a genuine connection to the music.

Community and Culture

The Rusty Nail has cultivated a family-like atmosphere under owner Sandy's warm hospitality. Many patrons describe feeling immediately welcomed - with the friendly staff and regular musicians creating an environment where everyone is treated like family. The venue has become a pilgrimage site for blues enthusiasts - with traveling jazz and blues musicians often stopping by to sit in during jams or festival events.

The Cape Fear Blues Society - based out of The Rusty Nail - has been active since 1987 and transformed into a larger all-inclusive organization in 1995. The society produces - promotes and presents blues music throughout the Cape Fear region - working alongside a vibrant network of blues societies across North Carolina to keep the blues alive and thriving.

History and Legacy

Originally opening as a watering hole in 1957 - The Rusty Nail has occupied its role as a blues institution since the mid-1990s. Before settling at its current location - the jam occupied various venues including Rockit's Sports Bar - the River Club and the Icehouse - but The Rusty Nail provided the perfect authentic juke joint atmosphere that the blues jam needed to truly flourish. The venue lives up to its name - maintaining a dive bar authenticity that blues purists appreciate while offering top-tier musical experiences.

Practical Information

Located at 1310 S 5th Avenue in downtown Wilmington - The Rusty Nail offers easy street parking for visitors. The venue maintains a cash bar serving cold beers and top-shelf spirits. While not focused on craft cocktails or extensive draft selections - the straightforward drink menu fits perfectly with the authentic dive bar atmosphere. The venue keeps its facilities clean and well-maintained - balancing the gritty blues bar aesthetic with guest comfort.
